title: Benchmarking the generalized Kadanoff-Baym ansatz and second-order adiabatic expansion using time-dependent spintronic effects: Spin pumping, torque, and inertia
authors: Jalil Varela-Manjarres, Nicole Sofia Salazar-Delgado, Branislav K. Nikolic
abstract: The generalized Kadanoff-Baym ansatz (GKBA) [P. Lipavský {\em et al.}, Phys. Rev. B {\bf 34}, 6933 (1986)] has emerged as a popular and numerically efficient algorithm for simplification of nonequilibrium Green's function (NEGF)-based calculations of time-dependent quantum transport. For systems that can be split into classical and quantum degrees of freedom, another popular simplifying strategy is adiabatic expansion (AE) of NEGF [N. Bode {\em et al.}, Phys. Rev. Lett. {\bf 107}, 036804 (2011); S. Deghi {\em et al.}, Phys. Rev. B {\bf 110}, 115409 (2024)] in terms of the velocity of classical degrees of freedom, such as localized magnetic moments (LMMs) in spintronics or coordinates of nuclei in nanoelectronics. Here we compare GKBA and second-order AE with numerically exact benchmarks for two-terminal junctions whose central region hosting quantum electrons and classical LMMs is attached to two semi-infinite normal metal leads. Three simple models are employed to exhibit cornerstone time-dependent effects in spintronics---spin pumping and spin-transfer torque (STT), as well as magnetic inertia as a recently explored phenomenon. We find that GKBA fails to describe pumping of spin current by precessing LMMs, or STT vectors, and thereby induced LMM dynamics. Conversely, the second-order AE matches numerically exact benchmarks for both effects remarkably well, thereby also revealing the essentially {\em nonadiabatic} nature of spin pumping. Thus, AE opens a path toward an accurate description of STT-driven magnetization dynamics, including combination with first-principles Hamiltonians, while incurring a fraction of the cost of time evolution of full NEGF. However, despite including terms up to the second time derivatives of LMMs into AE, this approach fails to capture fast nutational oscillations on top of the precessional motion of LMMs as the hallmark of magnetic inertia.
summary: This work compares three methods—full KBE, GKBA, and second-order AE—for simulating time-dependent quantum transport in spintronic junctions. The second-order AE proves to be a highly accurate and computationally efficient alternative to the full KBE for describing spin pumping and STT. However, the authors note that this approximation fails to capture the fast oscillations associated with magnetic inertia.
main_problem: The paper benchmarks different theoretical approximations for calculating time-dependent quantum transport in spintronic junctions, specifically comparing the Generalized Kadanoff-Baym ansatz (GKBA) against the second-order Adiabatic Expansion (AE).
main_result: The second-order AE accurately describes spin pumping and Spin-Transfer Torque (STT) effects, suggesting a nonadiabatic nature, while the GKBA fails to capture these dynamics. However, AE is limited in describing fast magnetic inertia oscillations.
method: The study uses the Nonequilibrium Green's Function (NEGF) formalism, comparing the full Kadanoff-Baym equations (KBE) against the GKBA and the computationally cheaper second-order AE.
model_or_system: The model is a two-terminal junction where quantum electrons interact with classical Localized Magnetic Moments (LMMs) in the central region, attached to semi-infinite normal metal leads.
key_observables: Spin current pumping, Spin-Transfer Torque (STT) vectors, and LMM dynamics governed by the Landau–Lifshitz-Gilbert (LLG) equation.
important_parameters: Time-dependent coupling strengths, the order of the adiabatic expansion (second-order), and the inclusion of magnetic inertia terms.
main_assumptions: The GKBA neglects certain memory effects, and the AE assumes the separation of fast quantum and slow classical degrees of freedom.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the computational scaling of KBE vs. GKBA. Figure 2 schematically shows three 1D toy models demonstrating spin pumping, voltage-driven STT, and magnetic inertia.
paper_structure: The paper introduces the physical setup and the computational challenges of KBE, then proceeds to compare the accuracy and efficiency of GKBA and second-order AE against numerically exact benchmarks for key spintronic phenomena.
why_interesting: The comparison of approximations (GKBA vs. AE) for non-equilibrium dynamics in coupled quantum-classical systems is highly relevant for developing accurate, yet computationally tractable, models for open quantum systems.
